Create your own buttons in Gladys, with a name, an icon and a colour, then
start a scene when you press them. No need to fake an MQTT device.

> Unofficial integration. **Tested with a fake Gladys only** (the automatic
> tests of the project), never yet on a real installation.

## The four types of button

| Type             | What it does                                                                                                                | Example          |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| **Push button**  | One press = one pulse: it goes to 1, then back to 0 by itself one second later.                                             | "Start movie"    |
| **Switch**       | On / off, remembered (even after a restart).                                                                                | "Night mode"     |
| **Timed switch** | On, then back to off by itself after the chosen duration (1 to 1440 minutes). Pressing "on" again starts the duration over. | "Heating 30 min" |
| **Selector**     | 2 to 6 named positions, one at a time, remembered; each position can start its own scene.                                   | "Heating mode"   |

A button **controls nothing by itself**: a scene acts when it changes. The
button is the remote, the scene does the work.

## Step 1: create the button

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**, then **Virtual buttons**, tab
   **Configuration**.
2. Click **Add a button**. A small form opens:
   - **Name**: for example `Heating` (up to 40 characters; the widget shows
     24);
   - **Type of button**: tick one of the four lines, each explained in one
     sentence. The type cannot be changed later;
   - **Duration in minutes**: for the timed switch only;
   - **Positions**: for the selector only, 2 to 6 names separated by commas,
     in order, 20 characters each at most; for example
     `Comfort, Eco, Frost protection, Off`, or the 6 orders of a pilot wire
     `Comfort, Comfort -1, Comfort -2, Eco, Frost protection, Off`. At
     creation, the selector is on the first one;
   - **Icon**: a list of 50 icons, each with a plain name, grouped by theme:
     on / off, switch, play, pause, stop, flame / heating, radiator, cold /
     frost protection, light bulb, shutter, plug, music, house, door, bed /
     bedtime, meal / kitchen, party… To **see them before choosing**, add the
     **Icons** widget (see below);
   - **Colour in the widget**: main (blue), secondary (grey) or danger (red);
   - **Ask for confirmation before pressing (widget)**: yes or no.
3. Confirm. Under the button, the message says: `Button "Heating" added. Now
open the Discovery tab…`.

## Step 2: add it to Gladys (Discovery tab)

Gladys does not let an integration create a device on its own: you approve it.

1. Open the **Discovery** tab of the integration.
   What you see: one **card** per button. At the top, the name of the button
   as the title; below, **"Features"** with a tag (**"Push button"** for a
   push button, **"Switch (On/Off)"** for a switch or a timed switch,
   **"Selection"** for a selector); then a
   folding link **"Technical parameters"**: that is the look of the button
   (icon, colour…), do not change it; at the very bottom, a green
   **"Add to Gladys"** button.
2. Click the green **"Add to Gladys"** button. The header of the card then
   shows the badge **"Already added"**.
3. The button appears in the **Devices** tab, with the same tag "Push button",
   "Switch (On/Off)" or "Selection".

## Step 3: the scene that acts

Open **Scenes**, click **New scene**, give it a name and an icon (the flame,
for example), then add a **"Device state change"** trigger and pick your
button in the device list. What comes next depends on the type.

### For a push button

What you see under the chosen device: a list of button events, and a toggle
**"Run the scene after the condition has been valid for:"**.

1. Choose **"Simple click"**. There is no value to type: the scene starts at
   every press.
2. Leave the toggle "Run the scene after the condition has been valid for:"
   **off**.
3. **Action**: for example **"Set device value"**, choose the plug of the
   heater and **switch its toggle on** (on = turn on).
4. Save and enable the scene.

### For a switch or a timed switch

What you see under the chosen device: two buttons **"On"** and **"Off"**, then
**three toggles**, in this order:

- **"Start the scene on any state change, whatever the value"**: leave it
  **off** (on, it hides "On" and "Off");
- **"Execute only when threshold is passed (and not at every value sent by the device)"**:
  switch it **on**;
- **"Run the scene after the condition has been valid for:"**: leave it
  **off**.

1. Click **"On"**.
2. Set the three toggles as above: only the second one is on. The scene then
   starts only when the switch goes from off to on, never twice in a row (nor
   at a restart).
3. **Action**: for example **"Set device value"**, choose the plug of the
   heater and **switch its toggle on**.
4. Make a second, identical scene with **"Off"** (same toggles) whose action
   switches the toggle of the plug **off**. For a timed switch, this "Off"
   scene also starts when the duration ends.

### For a selector

What you see under the chosen device: a list of operators, a list of the
positions of your selector (by their names), then the same toggles as for a
switch.

1. Choose the operator **"equal"**, then the position in the list (for
   example "Eco"). If a text field shows instead of the list, click
   **"Choose from the list of values"**.
2. Set the toggles as for a switch: only "Execute only when threshold is
   passed" is on.
3. **Action**: for example **"Set device value"** on your radiator or pilot
   wire, with the mode you want.
4. Make one scene per position (4 positions = 4 scenes). A position keeps its
   number even when you rename it: your scenes keep working.

### Loops

Do not make a scene that sends a command **back to the button that started
it**. The integration protects itself:

- a press, an "on" or a change of position repeated more than **20 times in a
  minute** on the same button is refused for the rest of the minute;
- the "off" of a switch is **never** refused; an "off" of a switch already off
  (and an "on" of a switch already on, or the position a selector is already
  on) is accepted without sending anything to Gladys, so without starting a
  scene again.

## Step 4: the "Buttons" widget on the dashboard

1. Open your **dashboard**, switch to edit mode, add a box and choose the
   **Buttons** widget (of the Virtual buttons integration).
2. In its settings, choose **1 to 4 buttons** (Button 1 to Button 4). No slot
   is mandatory: you can fill Button 2 and leave Button 1 empty, and the widget
   shows the chosen buttons in the order of the slots. With none chosen, it
   says "Pick at least one button in the settings of this widget". Only the
   buttons added to Gladys at step 2 are listed.
3. The widget shows one pill per button, with the chosen icon, name and
   colour:
   - pressing a **push button** sends a pulse; the message says "pressed", or
     the error if Gladys did not take it;
   - a **switch** that is on shows its colour (blue if you chose grey); off,
     it is grey. A press does what the pill shows: turn off a pill that is on,
     turn on a pill that is off (if the state changed meanwhile, the message
     says "already off" or "already on");
   - for a **timed switch** that is on, a line shows the time left
     ("Heating: 25 min left");
   - a **selector** takes one pill per position, The current
     position stands out: its colour and a tick, the others grey (no line
     repeats it). A press puts
     the selector on the position of the pill (the message says "already on
     Eco" when it was). A card holds 4 pills at most: a selector of 4
     positions takes a card of its own. A selector that has no room left for
     all its positions shows none (never half of them): a message says to show it on another
     card;
   - a **selector of 5 or 6 positions** takes a single pill, with its icon, its
     name and its current position ("Heating: Eco"). A press opens a list of its positions, the current one already
     chosen: pick one and confirm. This list needs a recent Gladys (the
     version where a widget button can open a small form); with an older one
     the press does nothing and the message asks to update Gladys. The
     "Devices" box works with every version;
   - if you asked for a **confirmation**, Gladys asks you to confirm before
     sending.
4. For more than 4 buttons, add several widgets. Gladys accepts at most 30
   presses a minute on the widgets of the integration, all widgets together.

The buttons also work in the usual Gladys boxes: the "Devices" box of a room
(a **"Push"** button for a push button, a toggle for the switches, a group of
buttons for the positions of a selector, or a drop-down list when they do not fit), and for the switches the
**"Quick actions"** box. There, the icon is the Gladys one: the
icon you chose only shows in the "Buttons" widget. **The confirmation only
exists in the widget**: the "Devices" box, a scene, the voice or an assistant
press without asking.

## See the icons before choosing: the "Icons" widget

The forms can only show text: the "Icon" list gives each icon a name, not its
drawing. In Gladys, a choice of an integration form (drop-down list or radio
buttons) holds a value and a name, nothing else: no room for a picture. The
mode screens with icons (thermostat, air conditioning…) are drawn by Gladys
itself for its own devices, and an integration cannot use them for its forms.
To see the drawings:

1. On a dashboard, in edit mode, add a box and choose the **Icons** widget (of
   the Virtual buttons integration).
2. In its **Page** setting, choose a page (1 to 5): each one shows 10 icons, in
   the order of the "Icon" list of the forms, with the drawing, the name shown
   in the form and the technical name.
3. Once you have chosen, you can remove this widget.

## Change or remove a button

- **Change a button**: pick the button in the list (or type its name if it is
  not added to Gladys yet). The other fields say "Unchanged" (duration: 0);
  change only what you want. The result message lists what changed ("icon:
  Flame / heating; colour: unchanged…"). The type does not change. A new
  duration applies at the next "on". A new name does not rename the Gladys
  device: rename it in the Devices tab too if you wish.
  For a **selector**, the field **New positions** replaces the list (empty:
  unchanged). A position keeps its number: rename it in place, add or remove
  at the end (moving or inserting a position in the middle is refused: it
  would change the numbers your scenes use). The current position cannot be removed: put the selector on
  another position first. Gladys gets the new names with the next Discovery
  publication (right after).
  The form keeps its values after a run: **reload the page** before changing
  another button. If you apply exactly the same changes to another button
  right after, the integration asks you to run the action again to confirm.
- **Remove a button**: it is **final** (the scenes that used it will not find
  it again). Type its name to confirm (and pick it in the list if you wish). A
  switch that is on is turned off first: its "Off" scenes run. Then delete its
  device in the **Devices** tab if you had added it to Gladys, and **edit the
  dashboard cards** that showed it (Gladys shows a settings error there
  otherwise). If you only delete the device in Gladys, the button stays listed
  in Discovery.

## Safety: read this before controlling anything important

- **A virtual switch can be turned off (or on) by others than you**: a "turn
  everything off" command, the voice or the chat ("turn off Heating"), a
  connected assistant, any scene, any dashboard (even a wall screen). For a
  **sensitive command** (gate, alarm, boiler, garage door), **never use a
  switch**: use a **push button with confirmation** in the widget, put the
  conditions in the scene (someone at home, time of day, alarm state…), and do
  not show this button in the "Devices" box of a public dashboard (it presses
  without confirmation).
- **The state of the button is not the real state of the device it controls.**
  "Heating: on" means you pressed, not that the boiler is heating. If the scene
  fails or the device does not answer, the button does not know. To see the
  real state, add a real sensor (a plug that measures power, a thermometer) on
  your dashboard.
- The buttons are **never** declared as lights, so a "turn off the lights" never
  reaches them. A selector is neither a switch nor a Gladys heating mode (it
  is a "Selection"): a "turn everything off" or a "set every radiator to eco"
  does not change it. For heating modes, the scene acts, with its conditions;
  the selector only says what you chose.
- An "on", a press or a change of position that arrives too late (Gladys has
  already shown a failure, after 5 seconds) is refused: nothing is sent. The
  "off" of a switch is always applied. A selector has no "off": all its
  positions are handled like an "on" (even a position named "Off").
- If the container of the integration is stopped, a press fails (Gladys shows
  it). A timed switch whose duration ended while it was stopped goes back to
  off as soon as it starts again. A restart or a reconnection never sends
  Gladys a value it already holds: your scenes do not start again.

## The alternative without this integration: a scene in "Quick actions"

If all you need is **a button that starts a scene**, Gladys already does it,
without this integration and without a container:

1. Create the scene (for example "Heating 30 min") and pick its icon in the
   icon picker of the scene (the flame, for example).
2. On the dashboard, add the **"Quick actions"** box (or the **Scene** box),
   then add the scene with the label you like.
3. A press starts the scene, with its icon.

This integration is mostly useful when you need a **state**: an on/off switch
that is remembered, or a switch that goes back to off by itself after a
duration.

## Limits

- 100 buttons at most, 4 per widget (add several widgets); a selector has 6
  positions at most. Up to 4, each one is a pill of the widget; with 5 or 6,
  the widget shows one pill that opens the list (a card holds 4 pills at
  most).
- No long press nor double press, no free colour nor button size: only the
  three colours of the widget.
- **The shape of the buttons is the Gladys one**: a pill with an icon and a
  name. An external integration draws nothing itself (no HTML nor CSS: Gladys
  renders the widgets from a list of components fixed by the core). So there
  is no **round on / off button**; the closest: a switch with the "On / off"
  (or "Switch") icon, in the "Danger (red)" colour if you want it to stand
  out. No **pull cord** (slider) either: the "Devices" box of Gladys only
  shows a slider for real functions (light, volume, shutter, fan, duration,
  charge limit…), never for a plain number, and the widgets of an
  integration have no slider at all. Using one of those functions would make
  the button pass for a real device (a "turn off the lights" would reach it):
  this module never does. Nor a **rotary knob**: Gladys only has a round
  dial in its thermostat box, for real thermostats.
  What exists is the **list**: the "Devices" box shows the positions of a
  selector as a drop-down list when they do not fit on one line (Gladys
  decides, depending on the width of the box), and the widget shows a list
  for a selector of 5 or 6 positions.
- **No icon of your own** on a button, a status line or a tile (ICO, PNG, SVG
  file): Gladys only shows the icons of its own set there, by their name (the
  widgets do have an image component, but it is a picture, not an icon). If an icon is missing from
  the list, ask for it on the GitHub repository: it can be added if Gladys
  has it.
- The integration does not start scenes itself: the state change of the button
  starts them (step 3).
- The widget updates at every press, and otherwise every 15 to 30 seconds.
- If the saved list is lost (a new volume), the buttons are rebuilt from the
  Gladys devices: a switch and a selector take back the value Gladys holds, a
  timed switch comes back off (its "Off" scene runs).
- Tested with a fake Gladys only: please report what does not work on the
  GitHub repository.

## Data

The list of the buttons, their state, the positions of a selector and the end
of a timed switch are kept in
`/data/virtual-buttons.json`, the volume of the integration. Nothing leaves your
Gladys. If this file cannot be read, the integration never overwrites it and
says so in its status.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Virtual buttons asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create your own buttons | `section` | No | 1. Click "Add a button" below: a name, a type, an icon. 2. Open the Discovery tab and click the green "Add to Gladys" button at the bottom of its card. 3. Create a scene with the trigger "Device state change": for a push button choose "Simple click"; for a switch choose "On" (a selector: "equal" and the position) and switch on only the toggle "Execute only when threshold is passed". 4. Add the "Buttons" widget on your dashboard. The button does nothing by itself: the scene acts. Never use a switch for a sensitive command (gate, alarm, boiler): a "turn everything off", the voice or a scene can reach it; use a push button with confirmation. Tested with a fake Gladys only. |

## How to install Virtual buttons in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Virtual buttons appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-virtual-buttons:0.1.4`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-virtual-buttons](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-virtual-buttons).

Virtual buttons requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Virtual buttons is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
